changes.text: 伦道夫起身，影射着富兰克林的话，为自己拒签致歉：尽管有压倒多数和德高望重的名字为这份方案背书。他说，他拒签是因为他认为方案交给民众的选择方式会使会议的目标落空：九个州将不会批准这份方案，混乱必然随之而来。他说，拒签不等于他要在会外反对宪法，他只是要保留按日后的判断、照自己的职责行事的自由。

Randolph rose and, alluding to Franklin's observations, apologized for refusing to sign, notwithstanding the vast majority and venerable names that would give the plan their sanction. He refused, he said, because he thought the alternative the plan presented to the people would frustrate the Convention's object; nine states would fail to ratify it, and confusion must ensue. Refusing, he said, did not mean he would oppose the Constitution outside the convention's doors; he meant only to keep himself free to be governed by his duty, as his future judgment should prescribe it.

接着几位成员各自说明为什么签。莫里斯说，他也有异议，但视此为能得到的最好方案，愿连同缺点照收；多数已经决定，他服从这个决定；方案一出手，其余考虑都会退居其次，问题只剩“要不要有一个全国政府”，否则便是无政府。他并指出，按所提格式签名，只关乎出席各州一致这一事实。汉密尔顿说，他希望人人都签：几个有分量的人若反对甚至拒签，可能点燃潜藏在可能很快消退的拥护热情之下的火星，造成无穷祸害；在无政府与动荡、和方案可能带来的好处之间，没有什么可犹豫的。威廉森建议，签名只限于随宪法呈交国会的那封信，这或许差不多同样可行，也能让一些不喜欢宪法的成员满意——麦迪逊注明，他所指的就包括布朗特；至于他自己，并不指望有更好的方案，对签名毫无顾虑。布朗特说，他本已声明不会以承诺支持的方式签名，但这个格式让他如释重负——他可以不承诺自己，只证明“方案是会议中各州一致的行动”这一事实。

Then several members explained why they would sign. Morris said he had objections, but this was the best that was to be attained, and he would take it with all its faults; the majority had decided and he would abide by that determination. The moment the plan went forth, every other consideration would be laid aside and the great question would be whether there was to be a national government at all — with anarchy as the alternative. The signing in the proposed form, he pointed out, related only to the fact that the states present were unanimous. Hamilton urged that every member sign: a few characters of consequence, by opposing or even refusing, might do infinite mischief, kindling the latent sparks that lurked under an enthusiasm for the convention which might soon subside — and that between anarchy and convulsions and the good the plan might bring there was nothing to hesitate over. Williamson suggested that the signing be confined to the letter accompanying the Constitution to Congress, which might do nearly as well and would satisfy some members who disliked the Constitution — Madison notes that he alluded to Blount for one; for himself, he did not think a better plan was to be expected and had no scruples against putting his name to it. Blount said he had declared he would not sign so as to pledge himself to support the plan, but the form relieved him: without committing himself, he could attest the fact that the plan was the unanimous act of the states in convention.

dispositions.rationale: 在 story.4 中英文的致歉之后补入伦道夫第一次起身时陈述的拒签理由：交给民众的选择方式会使会议目标落空，九个州将不批准，混乱必然随之而来。ev 增加 F-E29。

evidence.quote: He refused to sign, because he thought the object of the Convention would be frustrated by the alternative which it presented to the people. Nine states will fail to ratify the plan, and confusion must ensue.

dispositions.rationale: 在 story.5 中英文的布朗特之前补入威廉森的提议：签名只限于随宪法呈交国会的信，以照顾一些不喜欢宪法的成员，麦迪逊注明其中包括布朗特；同时补入威廉森本人不指望更好方案、愿意签名的表态。ev 增加 F-E30 和 F-E31。

evidence.quote: Mr. WILLIAMSON suggested that the signing should be confined to the letter accompanying the Constitution to Congress
For himself, he did not think a better plan was to be expected, and had no scruples against putting his name to it.
He alluded to Mr. Blount for one.

dispositions.rationale: 按补入的 F-E29、F-E30、F-E31 检查了全文。发现两处遗漏，已分别在 story.4（伦道夫的拒签理由）和 story.5（威廉森的签法提议及其所指的布朗特）中补齐，并更新了这两段的 ev。其余段落与这三条摘录没有冲突，未作改动。
